title: Zephyr Biotech - security & deployment pathways discovery
summary: Initial security posture discovery for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Focus on SOC 2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit/logging expectations, KMS options and retention policy. Customer leaning toward private for PHI/workflows but wants cost/ops tradeoffs clarified; scope to run a technical pilot and request SOC2 docs and SAML integration guide.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Jordan Hale: Share SOC2 Type II report and ISO attestation (by 2027-07-23)
Priya Nair: Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) and propose lab time for bench (by 2027-07-27)
Luis Ortega: Provide SAML config template and sample SSO metadata (by 2027-07-24)
Marcus Lee: Share internal threat model and list of regulatory constraints (by 2027-07-30)
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and security whitepaper
Set up 90-minute SE deep dive to discuss network/VPC & KMS options
Customer to provide sample dataset characteristics (no PHI in sample) and success criteria
Align on pilot scope (hosted sandbox vs dedicated pilot) and timeline (target start early Aug)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-21 16:00 UTC / Duration 44 minutes / Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood SE), Marcus (CISO Zephyr), Tanya (Platform), Samir (DevSecOps), Elena (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intro around the table, then we want to focus on sec posture and deployment constraints.
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus Lee here, CISO at Zephyr Biotech. We run clinical research workflows so lots of sensitive material, PHI in some flows. Looking at options - hosted, dedicated, or private - need to understand controls.
[00:23] Priya: Hi Marcus, Priya Nair, solutions engineer. We'll cover SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration. Feel free to interrupt with specifics.
[00:32] Tanya: Tanya, platform lead - mostly infra questions and ops burden.
[00:36] Samir: Samir, DevSecOps, hi.
[00:39] Elena: Elena product.

[01:00] Jordan: Cool. To kick off, Marcus, can you briefly describe your compliance needs and what the decision criteria are? Timing?
[01:12] Marcus: Sure. We are pursuing ISO 27001 consolidation across the company and we already have SOC2 in progress with auditors. For LLM use, need isolation guarantees for certain regulated pipelines, audit trails for model inputs/outputs, SSO integration with Okta, KMS for key control, and the ability to retain or delete logs per data retention policy. Timeline: pilot in 6-8 weeks, production in Q4 depending on vendor gating.
[01:40] Jordan: Understood. Typical. For isolation, folks often choose Dedicated or Private. Hosted is faster but needs strong contractual controls and audit evidence.
[01:49] Samir: Quick question — when you say KMS, do you support customer-managed keys in the hosted environment? We have an HSM-backed KMS for certain regs.
[01:58] Priya: Yeah, good point. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can integrate with customer KMS via bring-your-own-key for certain tiers — we have a few enterprise customers using AWS KMS with envelope encryption. Note: HSM direct integration for hosted is limited; if HSM-only is a hard req, Private is usually the path.
[02:22] Marcus: So HSM requirement pushes toward Private. But there's a cost/ops concern. How heavy is the ops overhead for private?
[02:30] Luis: Luis here. Private includes a control plane we can run in your VPC, or an on-prem package. For VPC-private we handle the control plane but persistent data and keys can stay in your account. Ops overhead varies — initial setup and network peering, but day-to-day we provide patches and automation; still more ops than hosted.
[02:49] Tanya: Do you have a model for RBAC that maps to our roles? We need support for least-privilege and separation between analytics and clinical teams.
[02:58] Priya: We have RBAC with role templates: admin, operator, read-only, model-deployer. It integrates with SAML/SCIM for group sync. Caveat: some fine-grained token-level restrictions are easier on Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports token scopes and route-level policies, but if you want per-user prompt redaction policies and strict network egress controls, Private gives more control.
[03:26] Marcus: Audit logs — how long do logs live? We have to retain certain telemetry for 7 years for compliance.
[03:33] Jordan: Seven years is an outlier but we've handled long-tail retention via our enterprise retention add-on; logs can be exported to customer S3 or GCS buckets and archived lifecycle policies applied. In Hosted we can export, in Dedicated/Private logs remain in customer-controlled storage.
[03:50] Samir: Is there an immutable tamper-evident audit trail, e.g., write-once storage or signed logs?
[03:57] Priya: For high assurance we support write-once object lifecycles and signed event logs; there are customers who ship to WORM buckets or a third-party log-store. We can also provide event-streams to SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo, Datadog).

[04:20] Elena: About data residency — some of our datasets must remain in EU. Do you have region controls for hosted?
[04:27] Luis: Yes, hosted regions are selectable; we have EU regions and partners for APAC. For strict residency and on-prem needs, Private is the guaranteed route.

[04:40] Jordan: Maybe helpful to surface a few typical decision patterns: customers with PHI who need HSM and SIEM-level control often pick Private; those who want quick time-to-value but still need SOC2 & KMS often pick Dedicated; if you want minimal ops and standard protection hosted is fine if contractual controls suffice.

[05:05] Marcus: Understood. Can we talk specifics of SAML and SCIM? Okta is our IdP. We need Just-In-Time provisioning and group sync, and we want to map Okta groups to RBAC roles.
[05:17] Priya: We do SAML SSO with metadata exchange, support SCIM for provisioning. Okta mapping to roles is supported. We sometimes see transcription shows it as S A M L—please send a sample Okta metadata XML and we can prepare a config snippet.
[05:33] Samir: Any gotchas with SCIM?
[05:36] Priya: SCIM requires HTTPS outbound and certain attribute mappings; some enterprise networks block SCIM provisioning endpoints — in Private we keep provisioning internal to the VPC. Also note that group sync latency is near real-time but not instantaneous.

[06:00] Marcus: Encryption in transit and at rest — are there FIPS 140-2 crypto paths?
[06:07] Luis: For Private and Dedicated deployed on specific certified hardware, we can enable FIPS crypto with HSM-backed key store in the customer account. Hosted can use cloud provider FIPS modules but explicit FIPS attestation may require Private.

[06:25] Jordan: Any constraints on network — egress restrictions, static IPs?
[06:31] Tanya: We proxy everything. If Redwood needs to access our model registry, we prefer private peering.
[06:36] Luis: Private supports VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink options. For Hosted we offer static egress IPs for allowlisting, but not full peering.

[06:50] Marcus: Can we instrument prompts/outputs for PII scrubbing before they reach logs? We want pre-log redaction.
[06:59] Priya: We have pre-request hooks and filtering pipeline — prefix masking, regex redaction, and custom policies. On Hosted you can enable Redwood-managed redaction; in Private you can run redaction locally before logs ever leave your environment.

[07:20] Elena: Query on model weights — do you store any customer models in a shared store?
[07:26] Jordan: Models are generally stored in segregated model registries per customer in Dedicated/Private. Hosted uses shared model artifacts but we support customer-uploaded private models for dedicated/private.

[07:40] Samir: About latency/cost tradeoffs — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated on 1k rps workloads?
[07:47] Priya: Ballpark: hosted optimized multi-tenant latency is slightly higher under peak; Dedicated gives more consistent p99s at scale. Cost varies — Dedicated has commit cost but lower per-token for sustained high throughput. We'll pull a benchmark sheet for a comparable model.

[08:05] Marcus: We need to see a risk matrix — what are common failure modes and mitigations?
[08:11] Luis: We'll put together a high-level threat matrix: data leakage via logs, misconfigured IAM roles, model prompt leakage via shared cache — mitigations: strict namespaces, KV cache isolation, encryption, and route-level policies.

[08:30] Jordan: Quick qualification — budget band, procurement timeline, who signs the contract?
[08:36] Marcus: Procurement signs at VP level; budget TBD but expected to be enterprise scale. Timeline: pilot approval in 6-8 weeks, procurement Q4.

[08:50] Elena: Who will need access from our side in the pilot?
[08:53] Marcus: Platform team + DevSecOps + one clinical lead.

[09:00] Jordan: Great. Any blockers we should know about today?
[09:04] Marcus: HSM and long retention are blockers. Also need to validate SOC2, encryption controls, and SAML flows.

[09:14] Priya: Noted. We'll provide the docs and config templates. Luis, can you walk through sample SAML metadata after this call?
[09:21] Luis: Yep, I'll send a step-by-step, and a SCIM example.

[09:30] Jordan: Let's capture the pilot options — quick hosted sandbox with privacy clauses vs dedicated pilot in customer VPC. Marcus, which do you prefer as a first step?
[09:41] Marcus: Prefer a hosted sandbox for speed but with BYOK and log export to our bucket so we can validate retention. If missing HSM, we can move to private for production.

[10:00] Priya: That fits a common pattern. For sandbox we'll scope ephemeral keys and exported logs. We'll need sample data shapes and expected QPS.

[10:10] Samir: We can provide sample payloads but no real PHI, will sanitize.

[10:15] Jordan: Ok we'll follow up with SOC2 artifacts and the SSO/SCIM config. Also propose a 90-minute SE deep-dive the week after next to discuss VPC/KMS specifics.

[10:30] Elena: Sounds good. A couple of last Qs: do you keep model input/output for debugging and for how long?
[10:36] Priya: By default, we retain request/response traces 30 days for troubleshooting, but enterprise retention and auto-delete policies can be configured; also you can opt-out of storing content and only keep hashes/metadata.

[10:54] Marcus: We need retention controls turned on and an SLA around deletion when requested.
[11:01] Luis: We offer deletion workflows and confirm via audit logs; but legal export obligations sometimes complicate things — we'll document the process.

[11:15] Jordan: Great. Let's recap — Jordan to send SOC2/ISO artifacts; Priya and Luis to prepare SAML/SCIM templates and SE deep-dive agenda; customer to share sample payloads and threat model. We target pilot kickoff early August.

[11:36] Marcus: Thanks. Quick note — please mark any artifact with sensitivity flags when you send.
[11:42] Jordan: Will do. Thanks everyone.

[11:50] -- end of recording --
